architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: The uncertainty probe establishes whether an interpretable, prospectively frozen S1C41 performance-mitigation experiment can proceed.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Pass only if verified specifications or measurements establish AC1920 and TK100 reactive functionality, equivalent weights, and water contents; the resulting reactive-group accounting and MDI/NCO:OH treatment are documented and frozen; component conditioning, moisture control, mixing order and duration, heating and conditioning history, sample age, hold-start definition, measurement sequence, homogeneity inspections, and failed-run rules are frozen; a numerical usable-viscosity interval and the uncertainty estimator, confidence level, independent-preparation unit, and decision rule for both SI endpoints are fixed; and a process-matched reference or state-control plan is established. The subsequent performance test must use at least three independent S1C41 preparations, directly measure the 120 C hold trajectory, and treat any one-point state normalization as secondary and conditional on demonstrated shared-shape compatibility.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Do not execute or interpret S1C41 as a performance test if reactive-group balance remains unauditable, any required process or statistical field remains unfrozen, no process-matched reference strategy is available, or homogeneity and measurement procedures cannot distinguish formulation effects from realization-state artifacts.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Uncertainty characterization before S1C41 preparation, followed only after a pass by a matched 120 C hold from 15 through 90 min with at least 15, 30, 60, and 90 min measurements.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Lower total modifier burden and full nominal axis coverage, but its 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the predeclared 3-10 wt% broad evidence region. It becomes preferable only if 2.5 wt% is prospectively accepted as adequate minor-axis coverage.
Full coverage with 5 wt% tackifier and a more interior 17.5 wt% acrylic level, but it adds modifier burden without direct evidence of superior local mitigation.
Uses stronger approximately 20 wt% acrylic composition anchors, but exact analogue proximity does not predict local hold stability and its 25 wt% modifier burden is higher.
Useful acrylic-only mechanistic control, but it omits the independently supported minor-tackifier axis and therefore does not satisfy the declared performance-mitigation intent.
Useful tackifier-only mechanistic control with low burden, but it omits the acrylic-like axis and cannot test the full mitigation strategy.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The demonstrated local failure is excessive 120 C hold drift: E5 had SI15-60=0.515 and SI15-90=0.931 versus E1 values of 0.095 and 0.168. Local E2 measurements also established large realization spread, so formulation effects cannot be interpreted without process and state control. Paper-derived rheological analysis showed that realization state primarily shifts viscosity scale within the original chemistry family and that a 120 C anchor can support conditional calibration, while also establishing that temperature-sweep behavior and temporal hold drift are separate observables. Curated PUR literature/database priors support an acrylic-like formulation region around 15-25 wt% and a minor tackifier region near 5 wt%, but these analogues define a candidate family only and do not predict S1C41 viscosity or stability. The conservative experimental-design rule is therefore to retain both supported axes for the declared performance-mitigation intent and, among full-coverage candidates in the selected region, provisionally freeze the lower-burden S1C41. This is not based on exact analogue distance and is not an exact-property prediction. The Skeptic's stoichiometry, process-history, statistical, and unmatched-reference objections are decisive for immediate execution, so the present decision is an uncertainty probe rather than a performance claim. The Robustness Adjudicator's conditional preference is adopted: S1C41 remains the downstream target, but it must not be prepared or interpreted until modifier reactivity and water content are verified, true NCO/OH treatment is frozen, process fields and statistical rules are predefined, and a process-matched reference strategy is established. S1C40 is not rejected because it is farther from an exact literature point; it is secondary because 2.5 wt% lies below the predeclared 3 wt% lower boundary of the broad tackifier evidence region. S1C39 and S1C11 remain mechanistic controls and are not substituted for the full mitigation experiment.

action_requests.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
action_requests.reason: Required first bridge from the measured rheology to design rules. It will establish whether state-aware modeling outperforms formulation-only modeling, whether one-point state calibration is justified, and how temperature response and hold drift should be measured without using validation evidence.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Recover the measured low-drift 120 C reference trajectory and deterministic descriptors so the prospective candidate can be judged against an original-system stability benchmark over the same time window.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Recover the measured high-drift reference trajectory that defines the performance failure to be mitigated, rather than optimizing only nominal viscosity.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify the run spread of the reactive-core anchor and determine how strongly replication or state calibration must influence candidate selection and adjudication.

action_requests.name: get_temperature_support
action_requests.reason: Confirm the measured temperature domain and local temperature-response descriptors for the candidate-space reactive-core anchor, preventing unsupported thermal extrapolation.

action_requests.name: inspect_formulation
action_requests.reason: Establish transparent reactive-core composition, MDI fraction, and existing modifier fractions before evaluating candidates that add or displace acrylic-like or tackifier-like material.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After establishing the local design objective, obtain the auditable mapping from the E2 reactive core to independent acrylic and tackifier axes, including the historical and claim boundaries needed to compare candidate IDs without treating their order as a rank.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Retrieve source-level acrylic evidence and limitations to distinguish coarse numeric loading anchors from noncommensurate viscosity or stability outcomes and to check functionality-related risks.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Retrieve source-level support and limitations for the minor tackifier axis, including the conservative below-about-10-wt% boundary, without interpreting that boundary as an optimum.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Hot-hold stability at 120 C using abs(SI) for 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 min, with preference for reduced positive drift relative to E5
Initial and nominal viscosity at 120 C, reported in the source measurement unit without inventing a unit
Temperature-response behavior within 80-130 C, including whether the candidate remains monotonic and locally compatible with the supported response structure
Realization and repeatability risk, including replicate CV, max/min ratio, and any one-point state-shift estimate supported by the state-aware analysis
Acrylic-like fraction relative to the externally supported coarse 15-25 wt% region and the conservative 30 wt% lattice limit
Tackifier-like fraction relative to the approximately 5 wt% analogue region and conservative 10 wt% upper limit
Combined-modifier fraction and distance from the E2 reactive-core-only anchor
Reactive stoichiometry and MDI fraction after modifier addition or core displacement
Modifier functionality and whether reactive-group contributions are known rather than assumed
Process feasibility, including mixing, homogeneity, moisture control, thermal exposure, and measurement timing
Extrapolation burden and quality of evidence supporting each active modifier axis
Information value relative to reactive-core-only, acrylic-only, tackifier-only, and combined-axis alternatives
counterfactual_checks: Compare the selected intervention conceptually with the E2 reactive-core-only node to verify that the expected information is attributable to an active modifier direction rather than candidate ordering.
Check whether an acrylic-only candidate in the same loading region would test the stability hypothesis with less stoichiometric or compatibility risk.
Check whether a tackifier-only candidate near the externally supported minor-loading region would provide a lower-extrapolation mitigation test.
For a combined acrylic-plus-tackifier candidate, verify that each axis is independently supported and that the combination does not exceed either conservative bound.
Check whether lower apparent drift could arise solely from a different initial viscosity or realization-state shift rather than improved temporal stability.
Check whether state calibration changes the candidate ranking; instability of ranking under plausible state corrections should trigger uncertainty resolution.
Check whether the candidate remains preferable when repeatability and feasibility penalties are applied rather than considering mean hold SI alone.
Check whether any proposed mechanism depends on rheology alone; retain such explanations as hypotheses requiring chemical or structural evidence.
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment that mitigates the established hot-hold viscosity-drift failure while retaining usable melt viscosity, remaining inside measured temperature/time domains and bounded acrylic/tackifier regions, and explicitly controlling realization, process-history, and stoichiometric uncertainty.
design_implications: Optimize hot-hold drift jointly with viscosity level rather than selecting the candidate with the most attractive single-temperature viscosity.
Use 120 C as the primary hold and viscosity anchor because it lies inside the measured 80-130 C support and matches the original E1/E5 hold comparison.
Carry the original 15-90 min hold window and evaluate at least the 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 SI values; do not import the external 4-10 h threshold as a local acceptance criterion.

Treat acrylic and tackifier loadings as independently supported intervention axes. A combined candidate is admissible in performance-mitigation mode if both axes remain within the evidence-bounded lattice and reactive stoichiometry remains feasible.

Treat the external 15, approximately 20, and 25 wt% acrylic values and approximately 5 wt% tackifier values as directional coarse-region anchors, not directly commensurate predictions of local viscosity or stability.
Use acrylic at no more than the constructed 30 wt% lattice boundary and tackifier at no more than 10 wt% as conservative extrapolation controls, not as claimed optima.

Preserve or explicitly recalculate reactive-group balance when modifiers displace reactive-core material; modifier functionality, water content, MDI fraction, mixing, thermal history, and elapsed time before measurement must not be silently assumed equivalent.

If the state-aware analysis confirms a master-curve shift with reliable one-point calibration, compare candidates after state calibration; otherwise require replication sufficient to estimate realization spread.
Freeze candidate choice, measurement schedule, loss definitions, and acceptance criteria before observing the physical result.
material_regularities_to_use: Measured temperature sweeps decrease monotonically from 80 to 130 C and are well described locally by Andrade-type descriptive fits; this supports interpolation within that range but not extrapolation beyond it.

E2 nominal viscosity varies strongly among runs at every measured temperature, so realization or process state must be separated from formulation identity before treating viscosity level as a material property.
Temperature response and temporal hot-hold response are distinct observables: a temperature sweep establishes instantaneous thermal dependence, whereas the 120 C hold reveals progressive drift.
The original hold data establish a large stability contrast between E1 and E5 without establishing a molecular mechanism.

planner.physical_failure_mode: Excessive time-dependent viscosity increase during a 120 C hot hold is the primary demonstrated failure mode: E5 shows SI=0.515 from 15 to 60 min and SI=0.931 from 15 to 90 min, versus E1 values of 0.095 and 0.168. Nominal viscosity alone is not a sufficient target because E2 also exhibits large run-to-run spread, with CV about 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios about 2.8-3.6 across 80-130 C.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: A standardized 120 C thermal-hold trajectory using the original support points from 15 through 90 min, including measurements sufficient to calculate SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 for 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 min
Initial or 15 min viscosity at 120 C so stability improvement cannot be achieved by accepting an unusable viscosity level
A temperature sweep within the established 80-130 C support, preferably at the original temperature nodes, using the same defined realization and thermal-history protocol
At least one predefined state-calibration measurement if the state-aware summary validates one-point calibration
Independent preparation or run replication sufficient to reveal whether candidate performance is smaller than the E2-scale realization spread

uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary does not support a stable master-curve shift or one-point calibration.

The 120 C viscosity lies outside instrument or process feasibility even when hold drift improves.
Temperature response becomes nonmonotonic or materially departs from the locally supported structure.
A candidate requires acrylic above 30 wt% or tackifier above 10 wt%, or otherwise leaves the constructed evidence-bounded lattice.
Modifier hydroxyl or other reactive functionality is unknown and prevents credible stoichiometric accounting.
MDI fraction or NCO/OH balance changes unintentionally when modifiers are introduced.
Process history, moisture exposure, conditioning time, or hold-start definition differs from the original references.
Homogeneity, phase compatibility, or sampling artifacts make the measured viscosity trajectory ambiguous.
An apparent benefit depends on comparing external percentages, temperatures, or multi-hour stability metrics as though they were directly commensurate with the local 120 C, 15-90 min test.
Candidate mapping does not permit an auditable distinction among reactive-core, acrylic, tackifier, and combined-modifier contributions.
No candidate offers a bounded performance-mitigation test with both acceptable feasibility and informative discrimination; in that case abstain rather than extrapolate.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates the demonstrated 120 C hot-hold viscosity-drift failure while retaining measurable and predeclared usable melt viscosity.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: For at least three independent preparations, the upper uncertainty bound on the candidate mean must be below the fixed E5 references for both SI15-60=0.515 and SI15-90=0.931. The 15 min viscosity must remain inside a process- and instrument-feasibility interval frozen before observing results, and the 80-130 C sweep must remain monotonic without phase separation, gelation, skinning, or sampling ambiguity. E1 values of 0.095 and 0.168 are a low-drift benchmark, not a mandatory pass threshold.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Reject the mitigation claim if either SI uncertainty bound is not below the corresponding E5 reference, if improvement is smaller than realization spread, if usable-viscosity criteria fail, or if uncontrolled process history, nonmonotonic response, stoichiometric ambiguity, or physical incompatibility makes the trajectory uninterpretable.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Matched 120 C hold from 15 through 90 min; static viscosity alone is not admissible as evidence of stability.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Replicated 120 C hot-hold viscosity trajectory in the source measurement unit, with primary SI=(eta_t1-eta_15)/eta_15 for 15-to-60 and 15-to-90 min; also record eta_15 at 120 C and an 80-130 C sweep at the original temperature nodes.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use the 15 min viscosity at 120 C as the predefined realization anchor because it is in-range and coincides with the hold test. Prepare at least three independent realizations under a frozen mixing, moisture-control, heating, conditioning, and hold-start protocol. Use one-point state calibration only as a secondary normalization after confirming monotonic 80-130 C behavior and acceptable shared-shape compatibility; do not use calibration to replace the directly measured hold trajectory.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 min, including at least 15, 30, 60, and 90 min measurements

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 has severe 120 C hold drift, with SI15-60=0.515 and SI15-90=0.931, whereas E1 has SI15-60=0.095 and SI15-90=0.168; this establishes the failure mode without establishing a molecular mechanism.

Measured local evidence: E2 viscosity has large realization spread across 80-130 C, including CV=0.585 and max/min=3.57 at 120 C, so nominal viscosity cannot be interpreted without replication and state control.

Derived model rule: within the audited local chemistry family, realization state mainly shifts viscosity scale while a shared thermal-response shape is transferable; one 120 C anchor gave roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative calibration error. Transfer to modifier-containing candidates remains unverified.

Measured local evidence and derived design rule: temperature-sweep response and temporal hold drift are distinct observables; mitigation must therefore be judged by a matched 120 C, 15-90 min hold rather than static viscosity.

External directly commensurate composition anchors: acrylic-like loading is repeatedly documented near 19-20 wt% of total formulation and at 25 wt%; tackifier-like loading is documented around 4.8-6.4 wt%. These loading anchors do not directly predict local viscosity or hold drift.

External directional or noncommensurate evidence: 15% acrylic is a lower-region prior with an uncertain fraction denominator, and the 25% acrylic stability comparison used different chemistry and a much longer 0.5-8 h window. These support a family or region, not an exact local composition.

Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported axes must be represented before applying minimum-modifier-burden tie-breaking; acrylic-only and tackifier-only candidates are controls rather than default performance choices.

Conservative design principle: use the 15-20 wt% acrylic initial band and approximately 5 wt% tackifier region before larger modifier burdens; exact distance to a literature percentage is audit metadata only.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate the demonstrated excessive time-dependent viscosity increase during a 120 C hot hold while retaining usable melt viscosity, using a bounded combined acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier-like intervention on the E2 reactive core.
unresolved_questions: What are the verified hydroxyl or other NCO-reactive functionalities, equivalent weights, and water contents of AC1920 and TK100?
Does proportional displacement of the E2 core preserve the intended NCO/OH balance after modifier reactivity is included?
What numerical 120 C viscosity interval defines instrument and process usability? This must be frozen before measurement.
Are AC1920 and TK100 homogeneous with the E2 core throughout mixing and the 90 min hold?
Does the local shared-shape/state-shift model remain valid for combined-modifier chemistry, or is replication without model normalization required?
What mixing order, mixing time, reaction temperature and time, conditioning time, moisture-control procedure, heating profile, sample age, and hold-start definition will be standardized?
Does the evidence support only the recommended 15-20 wt% acrylic plus approximately 5 wt% tackifier region rather than any exact composition? Current evidence supports the region only.
Can S1C39 and S1C11 be run alongside S1C41 to distinguish acrylic-only, tackifier-only, and combined-axis effects without claiming an unmeasured molecular mechanism?

robustness_checks.detail: S1C41 directly tests mitigation of the measured 120 C time-dependent viscosity increase using matched 15-60 and 15-90 min hold endpoints rather than static viscosity alone.

The declared intent is performance_mitigation. S1C41 covers both independently supported axes, acrylic_like and minor_tackifier_like; partial-coverage candidates are correctly retained as controls rather than promoted for lower burden.

Removing exact analogue-distance rewards does not disqualify S1C41: 15 wt% acrylic lies at the directional lower edge of the supported 15-25 wt% region and 5 wt% tackifier lies within the repeated minor-resin region. The exact 15/5 point is not established as optimal.

S1C41 is the lowest-burden full-coverage candidate with acrylic in the conservative 15-20 wt% initial band and tackifier in the approximately 4.8-6.4 wt% repeated cluster. S1C40 is lower burden, but its 2.5 wt% tackifier is below the stated broad 3-10 wt% evidence region.

S1C40 would be a cleaner lower-burden performance test only if 2.5 wt% tackifier were predeclared as adequately supported. S1C39 and S1C11 are cleaner causal controls but do not test the full performance-mitigation strategy.

All six major process fields are missing, E2 realization spread is large, and state-calibration transfer to modifier-containing chemistry is unverified. Uncontrolled process state could dominate an apparent formulation effect.

AC1920 and TK100 functionality, equivalent weights, and water contents are unknown. The true NCO/OH balance after core displacement cannot yet be audited, so drift changes could reflect unintended stoichiometric changes.

The recommendation does not rely on active-axis distance, which is audit-only. It follows measured-failure alignment, full axis coverage, bounded evidence regions, and lower burden within that region.

The replicated 120 C hold, both SI endpoints, initial viscosity, in-range temperature sweep, and homogeneity observations address the claim. The numerical usability interval, uncertainty method, confidence level, failed-run handling, and process-matched reference control remain unspecified.

The unresolved stoichiometry and process-history findings are serious enough to require an uncertainty-resolution step before executing or interpreting the S1C41 performance test, but they do not presently justify reranking to another formulation because the same process uncertainty affects the candidate set broadly.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not fully establish that S1C40 has materially poorer evidence coverage than S1C41; dismissing it mainly because 2.5 wt% is farther from the approximately 5 wt% analogue cluster risks using literature proximity as a ranking objective.
The ranking has not been shown to remain stable under plausible state corrections, even though the Planner identifies ranking instability under state calibration as an uncertainty trigger.
The claim that S1C41 is the minimum sufficient intervention is not supported by pre-result efficacy data; only its full-axis evidence coverage is established.
The proposed historical E5 comparison does not account for uncertainty in the single-run E5 benchmark or demonstrate process matching to the new candidate runs.

critical_findings.evidence: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 value applies only to the original reactive core. AC1920 and TK100 functionality, equivalent weights, and water contents are unknown, while S1C41 proportionally displaces the core and reduces MDI to 16.15 wt%. Without verified reactive-group contributions and recalculated NCO/OH balance, any drift change could reflect an unintended stoichiometric shift rather than the proposed modifier intervention.
critical_findings.issue: Reactive stoichiometry is not auditable for S1C41.

critical_findings.evidence: Every candidate scorecard reports six missing major process fields and high process-history uncertainty. E2 has CV=0.585 and max/min=3.57 at 120 C, and the shared-shape calibration was validated only within the original chemistry family. A three-preparation statement does not by itself control mixing order, moisture, conditioning, heating profile, sample age, or hold-start definition.
critical_findings.issue: The experiment remains vulnerable to uncontrolled realization and process-history effects.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 is also classified as full coverage with strong analogue support and has a lower total modifier burden of 17.5 wt% versus 20 wt% for S1C41. The stated reason for rejecting S1C40 is that 2.5 wt% tackifier lies below the repeated approximately 5 wt% literature cluster. That is defensible as an evidence-boundary judgment, but it is not evidence that 5 wt% is locally superior or sufficient for mitigating hot-hold drift.
critical_findings.issue: The rank-1 choice may partially reward literature-nearness over minimum burden.

critical_findings.evidence: No local modifier-containing hold data establish intervention sufficiency. S1C41 is the lowest-burden candidate selected within the proposer's preferred 15-20 wt% acrylic and approximately 5 wt% tackifier region, but it has not been shown to be a sufficient intervention. This must be labeled a conservative evidence-coverage rule rather than measured sufficiency.
critical_findings.issue: The phrase 'minimum sufficient perturbation' overstates what has been established.

critical_findings.evidence: The process/instrument viscosity interval is deferred for later definition, and 'upper uncertainty bound' does not specify confidence level, estimator, treatment of preparation effects, or handling of failed/ambiguous runs. The E5 thresholds are derived from one original run, so comparing a candidate confidence bound against fixed E5 point estimates does not represent uncertainty in the reference.
critical_findings.issue: The acceptance criterion is not fully frozen or statistically specified.

critical_findings.evidence: The approximately 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier records primarily demonstrate formulation feasibility or single-temperature viscosity, not local 120 C hold stability. The functional-tackifier stability context is confounded and near 19.8 wt%, not an isolated approximately 5 wt% result. Thus the second axis is a bounded pre-result hypothesis, not established mitigation efficacy.
critical_findings.issue: Independent evidence for the minor-tackifier axis is weaker for the measured failure mode than the proposal's coverage language implies.

critical_findings.evidence: The candidate-hypothesis tool discloses that the exact V2 grid and fine-refinement algorithm were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. The payload states that validation identity and outcome were excluded, but the absence of a contemporaneous freeze prevents independent confirmation.
critical_findings.issue: Prospective provenance cannot be fully verified.

However, the exact candidate grid and refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment, and no contemporaneous freeze artifact is available, so outcome-blind provenance cannot be independently verified from this payload.

Alignment remains qualified because tackifier efficacy against local hold drift is supported only directionally by external analogues, while modifier reactivity, stoichiometry, and process history remain unresolved.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
